For a long time, I assumed my AI skills were solid because they worked when things were calm. I could generate drafts quickly, summarize information accurately, and move through tasks faster than before. Nothing broke. Nothing raised alarms.
That changed the first time I had to rely on AI when the conditions weren’t forgiving.

Pressure exposes what’s real.

articles.author: CVE Reports
articles.description:
YAML Deserialization: The Gift That Keeps on Giving in Docling-Core



Vulnerability ID: CVE-2026-24009
CVSS Score: 8.1
Published: 2026-01-22
A classic remote code execution vulnerability in the docling-core library caused by the insecure use of PyYAML's FullLoader, allowing attackers to turn document processing pipelines into remote shells.
The docling-core library, used for processing and modeling documents, contained a critical vulnerability in its YAML loading mechanism. By explicitly using yaml.FullLoader instead of SafeLoader, the library allowed the deserialization of arbitrary Python objects. This means if you can get the application to parse a malicious YAML file, you can execute code on the server. The fix is a one-line change to SafeLoader in version 2.48.4.
CWE ID: CWE-502
Atta…
articles.title: CVE-2026-24009: YAML Deserialization: The Gift That Keeps on Giving in Docling-Core

articles.description:
Digital signatures are often treated as a solved problem. In practice, most systems solve identity, not integrity, and the distinction becomes critical once signatures are applied to structured data rather than static documents.
Healthcare is a good example, but the issue is not healthcare-specific. Any system that signs structured, interoperable data eventually runs into the same failure mode.
This post explains why that happens and what a correct signing architecture looks like.
Consider a common workflow:
A system generates a prescription encoded as structured data (for example, JSON).
A clinician signs it.
The data is transmitted to another system.
The receiving system re-serializes the payload:


Fields are reordered

Optional fields are omitted

Formatting and whitespace change
Signa…
articles.title: Why digital signatures break on structured healthcare data

articles.author: Sujit Kumar Bindhani
articles.description:
As a developer, I found myself spending more time searching for answers than actually building.
"Where are the requirements for this ticket?" "Did we update the documentation for the new API endpoint?" "Who worked on this module last year?"
My information was scattered everywhere: Jira for tasks, GitHub for code, Notion for docs, and Slack/Teams for decisions. I was constantly context-switching, acting as a human router for information.
I realised I didn't just need a "project management tool" I needed Project Intelligence.
So, I built ProjIntel.ai.
🚀 What is it?
ProjIntel.ai is an intelligent hub that connects your entire development ecosystem. It ingests data from your Codebase, Jira, Asana, Trello, and Notion, and lets you chat with it.
Instead of digging through five different tabs, you can just ask:
"What is the status of the auth refactor and which files are affected?"
...and it gives you an answer based on real-time data from your code and your task tracker.
🛠️ Key Features
Unified Context: It understands the link between a Jira ticket and the actual code in your repo.
Instant Answers: Ask questions about your project status, technical debt, or architectural decisions.
Automated Reporting: Generate status reports without manually copy-pasting from three different tools.
Security First: Enterprise-grade security to keep your proprietary data safe.
🎁 Try it out
I'm currently running a 15-Day Free Trial for the Starter plan. No commitments, I just genuinely want to see if this solves the "fragmented knowledge" problem for other teams as well as it has for mine.
check it out here: https://projintel.ai
I'd love to hear your feedback in the comments! 👇
articles.title: Stop Drowning in Context Switching: Why I Built an AI That "Talks" to My Jira, Codebase, and Docs
